hook: Robin Rombach is the lead author of the Latent Diffusion Models paper produced with the CompVis group at LMU Munich, the research that became the technical basis for Stable Diffusion. After a physics degree at Heidelberg and a PhD at LMU Munich, he continued the work as Research Director at Stability AI before leaving in 2024. In August 2024 he co-founded Black Forest Labs with two of his Latent Diffusion co-authors, Patrick Esser and Andreas Blattmann, releasing the FLUX.1 image model on launch day. He now runs Black Forest Labs as CEO from labs in Freiburg and San Francisco, and in 2026 spoke at the G7 alongside heads of state to argue for keeping frontier visual AI development open.

quick_facts: First author of 'High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models' (2021, with Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, and Bjorn Ommer), the paper underlying Stable Diffusion.
Studied physics at the University of Heidelberg (2013-2020) and pursued his PhD at LMU Munich in the CompVis group.
Served as Research Director at Stability AI before leaving in 2024.
Co-founded Black Forest Labs on August 1, 2024, with fellow Latent Diffusion co-authors Patrick Esser and Andreas Blattmann, raising 31 million dollars in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz.
Now Co-founder and CEO of Black Forest Labs, which builds the FLUX image and video generation models.
Spoke at the 2026 G7 summit to advocate for open innovation in visual AI, appearing alongside heads of state including President Macron and President Trump.
